title: Console RBAC v2: role assignment UI + guard sensitive pages/actions (feature flags + UX review)
creator: Chloe Martin
body:
Goal
- Deliver RBAC v2 role management UX in the Console and ensure sensitive Console pages/actions are consistently guarded (frontend + console-backend).
- Support staged rollout via feature flags (shadow -> warn-only -> enforce) with clear UX, supportability, and auditability.

Scope
1) Role assignment UI (Org Settings > Access / Roles)
- List org members (users + service accounts where applicable) and their current roles.
- Assign/remove default roles (no custom roles in initial GA; leave UI affordance for future but hide behind flag).
- Enforce separation-of-duties guidance via UI copy (e.g., Billing Admin vs Security Admin) and confirm dialogs for high-risk role grants.
- Show effective roles when multiple assignments exist (direct assignment + SSO group mapping) as a read-only summary.
- Include “last updated” and “changed by” fields when available from audit log API (or placeholder until ENG-5387 lands).

2) Guard sensitive pages and actions
- Ensure UI routing + page-level actions are hidden/disabled when not permitted, and that the console-backend returns standardized 403s with reason codes.
- Primary surfaces to guard (initial list; refine during implementation):
  - Billing: invoices, payment method, plan changes
  - Org settings: org rename, delete org, domain verification
  - SSO/SAML configuration: upload cert/metadata, enforce SSO, SCIM toggles
  - API keys: create/rotate/revoke
  - Audit log export / SIEM settings
  - Dedicated admin: autoscaling policies, GPU pool config (if surfaced in Console)
  - Private deployment admin (if applicable in Console): policy bundle version / updates

3) Feature flag + rollout strategy
- Flag names (proposed; align with platform flags naming):
  - console.rbacV2.uiRoleManagement (enables role management screens)
  - console.rbacV2.enforce (enforces UI gating and expects backend enforcement)
  - console.rbacV2.shadowDenyTelemetry (captures attempted actions that would be denied; no UX impact)
- Stages:
  - Stage 0: backend-only enforcement in staging; Console shows existing UI (baseline)
  - Stage 1: shadow telemetry (no blocking); log “would deny” events + client analytics
  - Stage 2: warn-only UI (banner/tooltip on restricted actions, still clickable but will 403)
  - Stage 3: enforce UI (hide/disable restricted actions; deep links show “You don’t have access” page)

Acceptance criteria
- Role management:
  - Org Admin can grant/revoke roles to users.
  - Billing Admin cannot grant themselves (or others) Security Admin / Org Admin.
  - Role changes are visible in the UI immediately after save (no multi-minute caching surprises); if eventual consistency remains, show a “changes may take up to X seconds” toast and poll.
  - For SSO-mapped roles: UI shows mapping summary (read-only) and links to the SSO settings page (if permitted).
- Guarding:
  - For each sensitive page, there is a definitive permission check driving:
    - sidebar nav visibility
    - route access (direct URL)
    - critical button/action enablement
  - Console-backend endpoints return standardized 403s with reason codes (align with control plane error contract).
  - Audit log events for role changes include actor + target + roles (or clear TODO until ENG-5387).
- Testing:
  - Integration tests cover at least: Billing page, SSO settings, API key create, role grant/revoke flows.
  - A “read-only” role can load dashboards but cannot access admin pages; deep links produce consistent “not authorized” UX.

Implementation notes
- UI permission model
  - Use backend-provided “viewer capabilities” endpoint (preferred) or embed permissions in session bootstrap payload.
  - Avoid duplicating policy logic in the client; client should consume a set of allowed actions for the current actor (derived server-side).
  - Where backend capability is not yet available, gate UI by minimal “role IDs” and keep logic centralized in a single permissions module.
- Error handling
  - Standardize unauthorized handling: dedicated “No access” page with request ID, reason code, and “Contact your org admin” copy.
  - Ensure 403s are not treated as generic errors in the console error boundary (avoid pager noise).
- UX review checkpoints
  - Midpoint review: navigation + role assignment table interactions (DES-241)
  - Pre-merge review: high-risk permission warnings and confirm dialogs
  - Pre-GA review: “No access” page copy, support diagnostics (request ID), and admin onboarding hints

Open questions
- Do we allow Security Admin to manage roles, or only Org Admin? Current assumption: role assignment is Org Admin only; Security Admin can view audit/export but cannot grant privileges.
- How to represent Support/Impersonation role in Console UI (likely hidden; managed only via internal tooling + break-glass policy).
- For Private deployments: do we need offline-friendly role management docs/UX differences, or keep Console consistent and rely on the same control plane abstraction?

Links
- PRD: PM-912
- Design: DES-241
- Related epic: ENG-5381
- Backend enforcement PR (console backend): see RBAC v2 console endpoint enforcement workstream (tracked under ENG-5385 / related GitHub PRs)

Rollout plan (Console)
- Staging: enable uiRoleManagement + shadowDenyTelemetry for all internal orgs
- Hosted canary: 5% orgs shadow-only for 3 days; monitor denial reasons + support tickets
- Hosted enforcement: ramp to 25% then 100% once shadow-deny discrepancies stabilize
- Dedicated/Private: coordinate with Connor (release/migration lead) and Solutions Engineering for enablement + comms; default to shadow until customer confirms role mapping
comments: 2025-02-07 (Chloe Martin): Kicking off console-side work as a parallel track to backend enforcement. Please keep client gating minimal and rely on server-derived capabilities where possible; we don’t want policy drift across TS vs Go.

2025-02-10 (Tessa Morgan): For role assignment table: recommend inline role dropdown with explicit “Save changes” CTA (avoid auto-save surprises). Also need a clear warning pattern when granting Org Admin/Security Admin. Adding copy suggestions to DES-241.

2025-02-11 (Naomi Feldman): Confirming phased approach: default roles only for GA. Custom roles are explicitly out-of-scope; please avoid UI elements that imply it’s available unless behind an internal-only flag.

2025-02-12 (Kevin Osei): For role change audit events, include both previous_roles and new_roles plus target principal type. If ENG-5387 isn’t ready, ship UI with placeholder ‘Audit log pending’ but don’t block gating work on it.

2025-02-14 (Jada Williams): Implemented first pass of permissions module + route guard for /settings/billing and /settings/sso in console-web. Next step is wiring to the backend capabilities endpoint; currently mocked for local dev.
2025-02-18 (Chloe Martin): Please add deep-link behavior: direct URL should not render partial page; should land on the standard NoAccess route and include requestId + reason code if present.
2025-02-20 (Connor O'Brien): Flag strategy looks good. For canary, we need a dashboard view of shadow-deny deltas (v1 vs v2) and a way to quickly disable console.rbacV2.enforce without redeploy.

2025-02-21 (Marcus Lin): Separation of duties: Role assignment must be limited to Org Admin at GA. Security Admin can view audit logs + export (subject to CISO decision), but cannot grant roles. Also ensure Support/Impersonation is not exposed in customer console.

2025-02-24 (Jada Williams): Progress update: role management screen skeleton behind console.rbacV2.uiRoleManagement is up. Route guarding for Billing/SSO/Org Settings is in place with a temporary ‘capabilities’ stub. Next: integrate real capabilities payload + add integration tests for deny UX.
